_comment: EXAMPLE FILE. Copy to flow-bridge.config.json (which is gitignored and never published) and replace every placeholder. Environment ids, org URLs and names below are placeholders, not real values.
Cowork Power Automate Bridge configuration.  v0.4.0, 2026-09-02.
TWO APIs, ONE AUTH. Delegated interactive auth (authorization code + PKCE on a
loopback redirect) now serves both surfaces, because the scope shape and the
per-resource token cache are identical for each:
DATAVERSE Web API (<org_url>)          -> flow DEFINITIONS: list/get/create/
update/delete/enable/disable
Flow service (api.flow.microsoft.com)  -> RUNS: trigger, history, per-action
detail, cancel, and connections
v0.1.0 aimed at api.flow.microsoft.com with client_credentials and failed for
two SEPARATE reasons that were then wrongly merged into one. Untangled:
- client_credentials IS unreachable. the author could not self-register an Entra app
(portal returns 401) and app-only would additionally need a Power Platform
admin. device_code is separately blocked by Conditional Access.
- api.flow.microsoft.com is NOT unsupported. The earlier note saying so
conflated the audience with the host. CORRECTED 2026-09-02: the AUDIENCE is
https://service.flow.microsoft.com (an identifier, no DNS record); the HOST
is https://api.flow.microsoft.com. Aiming a request at the audience gives
getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND, which is what produced the wrong conclusion.
Interactive auth against both audiences was proven end to end.
client_id is the public client Microsoft publishes in its own Dataverse developer
documentation so samples run without a private app registration. There is no client
secret anywhere in this design - a public client uses PKCE, so there is none to leak.
TOKEN CACHE
Set 2026-09-02 with the owner's explicit approval. The bridge runs stateless behind
supergateway, so the server is re-spawned per call and an in-memory token cannot
survive - without a cache EVERY tool call opens a browser. The file holds a REFRESH
TOKEN, is written mode 600, and lives under AppData, OUTSIDE the git repo, so it
cannot be committed by accident. Delete the file to force a fresh sign-in; set the
key back to "" to disable caching entirely.
HOW ACCESS IS DECIDED, in order:
1. the environment must appear in allowed_environments, with an org_url
2. production environments refuse EVERYTHING unless their id is in allow_prod
3. writes additionally need global read_only false AND no per-entry read_only
4. delete additionally needs allow_delete, plus confirm_name matching the flow
PRODUCTION IS FLAGGED, NOT GUESSED. v0.2.0 detected production from the NAME
alone. That is not sufficient here: "ProdCRM" is a production CRM whose name
contains no "prod", so it would have been treated as non-production and been
writable. Each entry now carries an explicit "production" boolean; the name
heuristic is kept only as a backstop for anything nobody has flagged.
WRITES ARE PINNED OFF EVERYWHERE EXCEPT THE DEFAULT ENVIRONMENT. Only the
default environment has had the full create/update/delete/state cycle proven
against it. Every other entry carries read_only true, so it can be listed,
read and analysed but not modified. Remove that flag on an entry, deliberately,
when you want to write there.
Only solution-aware flows are reachable through the DATAVERSE workflow table.
The Flow service sees more: list_all_flows returned 5 flows in the default
environment where the Dataverse list_flows returns 3. Use list_all_flows for a
true inventory; the Dataverse list remains the one you can create against.
RUN HISTORY - CORRECTED 2026-09-02. An earlier note here read: 'NOT AVAILABLE
... do not build a run-history tool without re-measuring first.' It was
re-measured, and it was wrong. The claim was true ONLY of Dataverse, where
flowrun, flowsession, processsession and workflowlog are all queryable and all
empty. Run history lives on the Flow service and IS reachable on this same
delegated auth - proven with real runs carrying status, timing and trigger name.
FLOW ENVIRONMENT IDs DIFFER FROM DATAVERSE IDs. The Flow service calls the
default environment 'Default-<guid>'. Passing the bare guid returns 403
EnvironmentAccessDenied, which reads like a permissions wall and is not one.
Any entry whose Flow id differs carries flow_env_id; the rest default to id.

allowed_environments.name: Default environment (writable sandbox)
allowed_environments._note: The Flow service calls the default environment 'Default-<guid>'; the bare guid returns 403 there. Prove the full create/update/delete/state cycle here before enabling writes anywhere else.

allowed_environments.name: Shared sandbox (read only)
allowed_environments._note: Listed, readable, analysable, never modified. Remove read_only deliberately when you want to author here.

allowed_environments.name: ProdCRM
allowed_environments._note: PRODUCTION. Flagged explicitly because a name-only heuristic would miss a production system whose name carries no 'prod'. Refused entirely unless its id is also in allow_prod.

_note: An environment you cannot read is not one this bridge should try to reach. Omit it rather than listing it read-only.
